raw_case_text:
A 39-year-old man presented with a 3-month history of skin lesions involving the face, neck and extremities. The patient was diagnosed as being HIV-positive a month earlier and was commenced on antiretroviral treatment abacavir 300 mg bd, lamivudine 300 mg bd and efavirenz 600 mg once daily, because of impaired renal function or pre-renal failure. The patient was hydrated with an improvement in the renal function. Two weeks after the development of the skin lesions, the patient complained of a sore throat and hoarseness of his voice.
On clinical examination, the patient had multiple translucent, clustered, umbilicated papules and nodules in the centrofacial region and neck with necrotic centres. In addition, there were verrucous plaques and nodules on the ears and upper limbs (Figure 1a and b). Chest X-ray was normal with no lung, hilar or mediastinal lymph nodes. A fibre-optic laryngoscopy revealed a supraglottitis with ulceration on the lingual surface of the epiglottis (Figure 1c).
Routine blood investigations demonstrated elevation of the liver enzymes with an infiltrative pattern (AST-63/ALT 70/ALP -219/Gamma GT-291). Abdominal ultrasound revealed an enlarged liver with abnormal parenchyma. The kidneys and the rest of the abdomen were normal. The initial CD4 count performed prior to the commencement of antiretrovirals was 2 cells/microL with a viral load greater than one million copies/mL. A repeat test (eight weeks later) showed a CD4 count of 124 cells/microL with a viral load of less than 20 copies/mL. Urinalysis and urine histoplasma antigen test were negative. Histology of the liver, larynx and sections of the skin demonstrated pandermal necrotising granulomatous inflammation. Grocott-Gomori methenamine silver and PAS stains revealed a relative paucity of intracellular oval, narrow-neck budding fungal organisms morphologically in keeping with Histoplasma capsulatum var. capsulatum (Figure 2a and b). Fungal culture of liver, epiglottis ulcer and skin confirmed the diagnosis of histoplasmosis.
On the basis of the clinical presentation, initial worsening of the disease and rapid elevation of the CD4+ T-cell count with lowering of the HIV viral load, the patient most likely has histoplasmosis associated IRIS. The patient was commenced on intravenous amphotericin B (0.8 mg/kg/day) for two weeks and continued with his antiretroviral treatment. He had an excellent response to this treatment and was discharged on itraconazole 100 mg twice a day.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 39-year-old HIV-positive man presented with a 3-month history of progressive facial, cervical, and extremity skin lesions, followed by a sore throat and hoarseness.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed cutaneous lesions over the face, neck, and extremities 3 months prior to presentation, followed 2 weeks later by sore throat and hoarseness. One month prior to presentation, he was diagnosed with advanced HIV (CD4 2 cells/uL, viral load >1,000,000 copies/mL) and initiated on abacavir, lamivudine, and efavirenz after hydration for pre-renal kidney injury.
subjective.past_medical_history: HIV infection diagnosed 1 month prior (baseline CD4 2 cells/uL, viral load >1,000,000 copies/mL) and resolved pre-renal acute kidney injury.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for facial/neck/limb skin lesions, sore throat, and hoarseness. Home medications: abacavir 300 mg BID, lamivudine 300 mg BID, and efavirenz 600 mg daily.

objective.physical_examination: Cutaneous exam: multiple translucent, clustered, umbilicated papules and nodules with necrotic centers over the centrofacial region and neck, plus verrucous plaques and nodules on the ears and upper limbs.
objective.routine_investigations: LFTs: infiltrative liver enzyme elevation (AST 63, ALT 70, ALP 219, GGT 291). Urinalysis and urine Histoplasma antigen test: negative. Chest X-ray: normal without lung, hilar, or mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Abdominal ultrasound: hepatomegaly with abnormal liver parenchyma and normal kidneys.
objective.advanced_workup: Immunology/virology: baseline CD4 count 2 cells/uL and HIV viral load >1,000,000 copies/mL; repeat at 8 weeks of ART showed CD4 124 cells/uL and viral load <20 copies/mL. Fiber-optic laryngoscopy: supraglottitis with ulceration on the lingual surface of the epiglottis. Biopsies of skin, epiglottic ulcer, and liver: pandermal/tissue necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with intracellular oval, narrow-neck budding yeasts on GMS and PAS stains consistent with Histoplasma capsulatum var. capsulatum.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Disseminated cutaneous, laryngeal (epiglottic), and hepatic histoplasmosis-associated immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) in a patient with HIV/AIDS. Confirmation: GMS and PAS staining of skin, epiglottis, and liver biopsies demonstrating narrow-neck budding yeast forms, and positive fungal cultures from liver, epiglottis ulcer, and skin confirming Histoplasma capsulatum var. capsulatum (despite negative urine Histoplasma antigen). Plan & clinical course: Treated with IV amphotericin B (0.8 mg/kg/day for 2 weeks) while continuing ART, achieving an excellent clinical response, and discharged on oral itraconazole 100 mg BID.
